purpose: Preserve documented alternatives for possible future human-authored amplified editions; never substitute these interpretations into the LBF base text automatically.

notes.baseWording: tomó a una hija de Leví
notes.basis: The narrative context identifies the taking as marriage, but the Hebrew surface uses the verb «tomó» without an explicit word for wife.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The approved base preserves the source wording rather than inserting the contextual relationship into the line.

notes.possibleInterpretation: the visible quality later emphasized in Acts 7:20 and Hebrews 11:23 may include beauty or comeliness
notes.basis: Human consideration raised during adjudication; it was not treated as authorized packet evidence and did not change the closed source policy.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The Hebrew surface טוֹב supports the broader direct wording «bueno»; «hermoso» would select a narrower contextual interpretation.

notes.baseWording: un arca de papiro, y la recubrió con betún y brea
notes.possibleInterpretation: the small ark was a chest or basket-like vessel made from papyrus or reeds and waterproofed with asphaltic materials
notes.basis: תֵּבָה permits ark, chest, or box; גֹּמֶא permits rush, reed, or papyrus; חֵמָר permits bitumen or asphalt, while זֶפֶת is pitch.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The base preserves the shared תֵּבָה wording as «arca» and names the materials without expanding the vessel's inferred shape or purpose.

notes.basis: The passive construction concerns what would be done to him; in context this would determine what happened to him.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The broader event wording would erase the source's passive action.

notes.possibleInterpretation: lo dejó con vida or no permitió que fuera destruido
notes.basis: The construction חמל על is used for sparing or preserving someone; here it follows her seeing the crying child.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: «Le perdonó la vida» states the resulting action more explicitly, while «lo perdonó» incorrectly suggests absolution of a fault.

notes.baseWording: golpeó al egipcio y lo escondió en la arena
notes.possibleInterpretation: Moisés mató al egipcio y escondió su cuerpo
notes.basis: The subsequent concealment and later narrative references establish the lethal outcome in context.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The base preserves the source verb «golpeó» rather than inserting the result into that verb.

notes.baseWording: dijo al malvado: «¿Por qué golpeas a tu compañero?»
notes.possibleInterpretation: dijo al que hacía la injuria
notes.basis: The man is characterized as רָשָׁע in view of his aggression against his companion; RV09 was raised during human review as an interpretive rendering.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The Hebrew contains a substantivized adjective, «the wicked one», not a participial relative clause or a noun meaning injury.

notes.baseWording: como un hombre gobernante y juez sobre nosotros? ¿Dices que me matarás
notes.possibleInterpretation: ¿Quién te puso por gobernante y juez sobre nosotros? ¿Piensas matarme
notes.basis: The first clause describes the kind of man Moses was allegedly appointed to be; the second challenges whether his words signal an intention to kill.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: The interpretive wording would omit explicit אִישׁ and replace the participle of «decir» with a cognition verb absent from the source.

notes.baseWording: Y vio Dios a los hijos de Israel, y supo Dios
notes.possibleInterpretation: Dios miró a los israelitas y los tuvo en cuenta
notes.basis: This interpretive rendering was raised during human adjudication through comparison with the NASB. In context, ידע may communicate God's full awareness and regard for Israel's condition, but the Hebrew clause וידע אלהים has no expressed object.
notes.reasonExcludedFromBase: «Miró» gives ראה a more intentional nuance, while «los tuvo en cuenta» supplies Israel as the second verb's object and replaces knowing with its inferred contextual consequence.
